newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says EU member omission "not end of world".
newsitem.headline: Turkey says EU member omission "not end of world".

text.p: Foreign Minister Ismail Cem said on Friday that Turkey was not overly discouraged by being omitted from a list of six nations favoured to join the European Union next.
"It is not the end of our world. Our future has not been darkened," Cem told a news conference. He said sidelining Turkey would also be to the detriment of the EU.
"If an injustice has been done to us, and I think it has, then it's also a problem for those who have done the injustice," he said.
The European Commission, the bloc's Brussels-based executive, recommended this week that the EU open negotiations in early 1998 with six out of 10 European countries seeking EU membership.
Turkey, struggling with economic problems, a poor human rights record and frequently in dispute with EU member Greece, was not on the list.
Cem said Ankara would not give up on its decades-old quest for acceptance in Europe. "Full membership of the EU is a basic desire of both this ministry and myself personally."
